patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and Salesloft share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Hunter and Salesloft share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Hunter only if your buying job matches “Domain email finder, verifier, and cold email sequences (All-in-one) — Free 50 credits; St” rather than Salesloft's shape. Choose Salesloft only if your buying job matches “Enterprise sales engagement / revenue generation platform — bi-directional CRM sync, seque” rather than Hunter's shape. Workflow advantage: Hunter leans email-outreach, data-enrichment; Salesloft leans sales-engagement, lead-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and Salesloft share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Hunter is Domain email finder, verifier, and cold email sequences (All-in-one) — Free 50 credits; Starter from $49/mo.; Salesloft is Enterprise sales engagement / revenue generation platform — bi-directional CRM sync, sequencing, coaching; talk-to-sales pricing..
- Company-size focus: Hunter (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Salesloft (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Hunter-leaning email-outreach, data-enrichment vs Salesloft-leaning sales-engagement, lead-management.
- Researched limits: Hunter — Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database; Salesloft — Not a contact database peer — weak as SI data/enrichment core.

Limitations — Hunter: Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database; Lead scoring is limited versus enterprise SI platforms; Salesloft: Not a contact database peer — weak as SI data/enrichment core; No published dollar pricing — talk-to-sales only.

Poor-fit cases: Hunter is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database · Salesloft is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a contact database peer — weak as SI data/enrichment core · Avoid Hunter if you actually need Salesloft's motion (Enterprise sales engagement / revenue generation platform — bi-directional CRM s)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
